A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Probabilistic Retrofitting of Learned Simulators. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original experiments on single-system and foundation models, including quantitative comparisons, rollout examples, hyperparameter ablations, and diffusion comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds energy-score evaluations and a deterministic deep-ensemble comparison.

M1.justification: The noise-injection mechanism, conditional normalisation, fair-CRPS objective, backbone adaptations, and Algorithms 1–5 are unchanged. Deep ensembles are an added comparator, not a modification of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Rayleigh–Benard, Euler, Shear Flow, Turbulent Radiative Layer, and Viscoelastic datasets and regimes. The new evaluations reuse existing coverage; they introduce no new task or data domain.

E2.justification: New Appendix E.3.1 and Table 19 add deterministic deep ensembles for Walrus and Lola on Rayleigh–Benard and Euler. Existing deterministic and diffusion comparisons remain; the diffusion discussion moves to E.3.2.

E3.justification: v2 adds energy score as an evaluation metric for single-system models and HalfWalrus. It also introduces a four-run deep-ensemble comparison, reported to require four times one CRPS run's compute. Existing splits, rollout horizons, and training configurations are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new deep-ensemble analysis tests whether improvements arise from CRPS training beyond ensembling alone. Figures 7 and 20 additionally examine whether marginal-score gains extend to multivariate evaluation. Existing hyperparameter ablations, ensemble-scaling analyses, and rollout examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports four separate fine-tuning runs with different initialisations for the deep-ensemble comparator. This is comparator-specific run information, not increased replication of CRPS experiments. The existing 100-iteration bootstrap procedure and confidence-level conventions remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 7 and 20 add energy-score improvements, and Table 19 adds deep-ensemble results; for example, Walrus/Euler VRMSE is 0.273 for CRPS versus 0.369 for deep ensembles. Original tables remain unchanged. Some new CRPS summaries differ from retained figures: Figure 7 reports 52.2% improvement for Walrus/Euler, while Figure 2 still reports 53.9%, without an explained setting change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and formal reasoning are unchanged. Energy score is introduced empirically without a new mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient architecture-agnostic probabilistic retrofitting, predictive improvements, and inference-time ensemble scaling. The additional evidence does not redefine the stated contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets energy-score improvements as evidence that univariate gains extend to multivariate performance. Section 5.3 and Appendix E.3.1 additionally attribute gains largely to the CRPS objective rather than ensemble presence alone. Existing architectural limitations and rollout-instability qualifications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new comparator's construction through four separate fine-tuning runs and its claimed fourfold computational cost. Existing implementation descriptions, hyperparameter tables, hardware information, and code-access information remain unchanged; detailed energy-score implementation information is not added.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are unchanged. The Fortin et al. reference receives author-list and page-range corrections, but its title and DOI identify the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v2 renames Section 4, expands selected results paragraphs, and reorganises Appendix E.3 into deep-ensemble and diffusion comparisons. Acknowledgements and bibliographic text receive local edits; the broader narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two energy-score figures, numbered 7 and 20, and the deep-ensemble Table 19. Existing displays are retained with subsequent renumbering and local reflow, including Table 9 moving to the next page. There is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The energy-score evaluations and deep-ensemble comparison provide useful validation absent from v1, addressing multivariate predictive quality and benefits beyond simple ensembling. The improvement is limited by sparse new protocol details and overly broad attribution and significance wording: Walrus/Rayleigh–Benard CRPS is 0.050 versus 0.051 for deep ensembles with overlapping intervals. Unexplained differences between new and retained CRPS summaries also reduce clarity, but the added evidence provides a modest net benefit.
